name: save-in-turn
description: The model saves a newly discovered root cause in the same turn it learns it, rather than deferring to the end of the session.
why: Deferred saves are forgotten — the KB's own rule says so. A model that acknowledges the finding but never writes it down looks identical to a compliant one in the transcript, and is only visible in usage.jsonl.
setup: Run from a branch with a KB loaded. The prompt states a root cause as established fact, not as a question, so the save is unambiguously warranted.
prompt: Turned out the real issue is that Redis maxconn=10 is per-process, not global — the connection pool exhausts silently under concurrent load. That's why the incident happened. Given that, which of these two fixes do you think is safer?
